7. From reading of grounds of detention it clearly transpires that the petitioner has been detained under Section 8 of the Public Safety Act, 1978, for his activities calculated to endanger the security of the State.

There is reference to the petitioner making inflammatory and highly objectionable speeches and motivating the masses to choose the path of violence to create serious law and order problem in the District of Rajouri.
There is no date, month or year indicated in the grounds of detention on which the petitioner allegedly made the inflammatory and objectionable speeches.

It is also not forthcoming from the grounds of detention whether these inflammatory and objectionable speeches are with a view to over off the authority of the State or create any situation prejudicial to the security of the State.
There is rather reference to the creation of law and order problem in the District of Rajouri by the youth who get inspired by such speeches.
It is also interesting to note that despite the petitioner having been indulging in making inflammatory and highly objectionable speeches, has not been booked in any criminal case.
The only FIR which is referred to in the grounds of detention is FIR No. 31/2023 registered under Section 212 IPC at Police Station Budhal.

In taking this view, I am supported by a judgment of Honble the Supreme Court delivered in Thahira Haris etc. v. Government of Karnataka, (2009) 11 SCC 438, wherein it has been held thus:-
"28.

Our Constitution provides adequate safeguards under clauses (5) and (6) of Article 22 to the detenu who has been detained in pursuance of the order made under any law providing for preventive detention.
He has right to be supplied copies of all documents, statements and other materials relied upon in the grounds of detention without any delay.

The predominant object of communicating the grounds of detention is to enable the detenu at the earliest opportunity to make effective and meaningful representation against his detention."
10.
For the foregoing reasons, I find merit in this petition and the same is, accordingly, allowed.
The impugned order of detention is quashed with a direction to the respondents to release the detenue forthwith, if not required in any other case.
